text:
Maya: :sos: Heads up — canary (us-west2) started hitting OOMs after the prefetched-window rollout (PR #12345). 6 distinct OOMs in the last 10m. Logs show big KV allocations on long prompts. Rolling back now.

Lucas: Seen it too, reproducing locally with seqlen ~12k. Profiling shows heaplet growth coincident with prefetch enqueue. Kernel routing flips more often; might be causing cache miss storms.

Erin: Bisecting the PR range. Quick note: commit 9f8a3b changed prefetch head/tail accounting and introduced a hysteresis for sequence-length-driven prefetch. Suspect the window calc bug.

Tasha: CI flagged memory regression earlier today: linux-release-x86-alloc/seqlen=16384 +22% RSS. CI link: <ci/reports/9876> (see heap profile).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated for canary group 'soft-prefetch-rollout' (deploy 2026-03-18T12:45Z) :arrow_double_left:

Carlos: Quick mitigation: we can set env PREFETCH_WINDOW=0 in canary to disable soft prefetch while keeping autobatch. Patch ready if ops agrees.

Maya: Apply the PREFETCH_WINDOW=0 to canary and staging, please. Also enable jemalloc_stats and add a heap sampling trace for kernel-routing decisions.

Lucas: Sample output snippet I pulled from a failing run: `KV_CACHE slab_free=18MB -> slab_used spike, slab_frag=36%, kv_entries=1.2M, ctx_len=12288` — looks like prefetch pushes many KV allocations that never coalesce.

Erin: Confirmed: reverting PR 12345 (see PR 12367) and re-running canary. If revert stabilizes, we will open a follow-up that fixes the window calc and adds unit tests around head/tail wrap.

Tasha: Note: small % of requests combine a very long system prompt and an immediate completion; that pattern triggers full prefetch + aggressive eviction, causing fragmentation. Might need sequence-length bucketing in the prefetcher.

Maya: Good call. If revert doesn't resolve, postmortem. For now owners: @Lucas (lead bisect), @Erin (revert/fix), @Tasha (canary monitor).

ops-bot: canary status: OOMs 6 -> 0 after revert (13m). Rolling status to :white_check_mark: stable.

Lucas: I'll follow up with a microbenchmark comparing PREFETCH_WINDOW values and kernel-selector traces; posting numbers to the infra perf board.

Erin: Also adding regression test: run long-seqlen synthetic workload with PREFETCH_WINDOW=3/0/6 across kernels to catch this in CI.

Maya: Thanks team — keep updates here. If you see any tail-latency or memory blips, tag this thread.
